question: Where do nursing research ideas usually begin?

options.A: A personal financial grant from the hospital board
options.B: An unanswered question or gap in nursing knowledge
options.C: The personal opinion of the chief medical director
options.D: A mandatory command from the ministry of health

explanation: Every good study starts when we spot a gap in our knowledge—something we need to figure out so we can take better care of our patients. You've got this! [learn more](GNS217_U3_T4#GNS217_U3_T4_h1)

question: Why do nursing students need to choose their research topics carefully?

options.A: So the hospital management can pay for their tuition
options.B: Because clinical time and research resources are limited
options.C: To completely eliminate all diseases from the ward
options.D: To ensure the final paper is published in a foreign journal

explanation: Time and materials are precious when you're balancing ward work and studies, so picking a focused topic helps you make every effort count! [learn more](GNS217_U3_T4#GNS217_U3_T4_h1)

question: What is the main goal of a clinically useful research problem?

options.A: Nursing care and patient health outcomes
options.C: The personal salary of the lead researcher
options.D: The architectural design of the hospital

explanation: At the end of the day, nursing research is all about making patient care safer and helping people recover better. That's why we do it! [learn more](GNS217_U3_T4#GNS217_U3_T4_h2)

question: When is a nursing research topic considered to lack practical value?

options.A: If it fails to include at least five different hospitals
options.B: If it uses complex laboratory equipment
options.C: If it fails to change or improve current clinical practice
options.D: If it generates millions of naira in profit

explanation: If the findings don't help us care for patients better at the bedside, the study misses the main point of nursing research. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T4#GNS217_U3_T4_h2)

question: What does a 'feasible' research project mean for a student?

options.A: Whether the hospital will change its name after the study
options.B: Whether the research topic is popular on social media
options.C: How many international awards the study might win
options.D: Whether the study can actually be done with available resources

explanation: Feasibility is just about being realistic—making sure you have enough time, money, and materials to finish the study without burning out. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T4#GNS217_U3_T4_h3)

question: A student wants to study a rare tropical disease requiring expensive lab kits, but has no funding. Which check is this study failing?
explanation: Even if a topic is super exciting, lack of funds and materials makes it unfeasible to carry out right now. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T4#GNS217_U3_T4_h3)

question: Which of these is NOT allowed when conducting ethical nursing research?

options.A: Forcing patients to participate to get a large sample size
options.B: Protecting the privacy and confidentiality of patients
options.C: Ensuring participants are protected from physical harm
options.D: Obtaining informed consent from every participant

explanation: Participation in research must always be totally voluntary. Patients should never feel pressured or forced to join! [learn more](GNS217_U3_T4#GNS217_U3_T4_h4)

question: Why do we need special care when doing research with vulnerable groups?

options.A: To prevent exploitation and protect them from harm
options.B: Because they always pay large amounts of money
options.D: So the researcher can finish data collection quickly

explanation: Vulnerable patients need extra protection because they might easily feel pressured to agree to a study. Keeping them safe is our top priority. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T4#GNS217_U3_T4_h4)

question: Why is having a personal interest in your research topic important?

options.A: It removes the need for formal ethical approval
options.B: It makes the data analysis process completely automatic
options.C: It gives the researcher motivation to complete the demanding project
options.D: It automatically guarantees funding from the government

explanation: Research writing can get tough! Genuine curiosity and passion for your topic are what keep you going through the late nights. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T4#GNS217_U3_T4_h5)

question: Besides personal interest, what else does a researcher need for their chosen topic?

options.A: A personal relationship with the hospital director
options.C: Relevant clinical expertise and methodological skills
options.D: At least ten years of experience living abroad

explanation: You need to understand the clinical setting and know how to collect and look at your data properly to get trustworthy results. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T4#GNS217_U3_T4_h5)

question: What does 'novelty' mean when picking a research topic?

options.A: The topic has already been researched a thousand times
options.B: The research project is written in the form of a novel
options.C: The study adds new knowledge or a fresh perspective to the field
options.D: The study uses brand new computers purchased from abroad

explanation: Novelty simply means bringing a fresh idea or a new angle to nursing so our profession keeps moving forward! [learn more](GNS217_U3_T4#GNS217_U3_T4_h6)

question: Why is it discouraged to repeat an overly studied topic without a new angle?

options.A: It fails to contribute meaningful new knowledge to nursing
options.B: It is illegal under international copyright laws
options.C: It automatically causes patients to reject treatment
options.D: It requires more expensive laboratory equipment

explanation: If we just copy old studies without adding anything new, we aren't helping evidence-based practice grow. Let's aim for fresh insights! [learn more](GNS217_U3_T4#GNS217_U3_T4_h6)

question: What does it mean for a research problem to be measurable?

options.A: The results can be guessed without collecting any data
options.B: Every patient in the hospital must agree with the findings
options.C: Its concepts can be clearly quantified using valid tools or scales
options.D: It can be measured using a simple household ruler

explanation: A measurable problem means you can use clear tools, scores, or observations to track and analyze your study variables accurately. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T4#GNS217_U3_T4_h7)

question: A nurse wants to study past unconscious ICU dreams, but no records exist. Which research requirement is missing?
explanation: If the information you need doesn't exist or can't be gathered, you won't be able to carry out that specific study. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T4#GNS217_U3_T4_h7)
